look_here_first: Annual bitterweed nearly identical in habit to var. amarum but with a reddish-brown to purple disk center beneath yellow drooping rays.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Hays-local source; Kew accepts Helenium amarum var. badium; Texas A&M notes the dark-centered variety in more central/western calcareous soils.
project_inclusion.range_guardrail: Installed for active visual learning; broader exact-county reconciliation deferred.

morphology_keys.family_pattern: Asteraceae/Helenium: composite heads with a raised receptacle, yellow or partly darkened rays, and often winged stems from decurrent leaf bases. Habit, stem wings, disk shape/color, and ray form are high-value characters.
best_field_traits: rays often bend downward at maturity
disk florets reddish-brown to purple distally
often associated with calcareous central/western Texas soils
morphology_keys.comparison_training: Think dark-centered bitterweed. The plant can look nearly identical to var. amarum until flowering; the disk color is the quickest field cue.
